intro: North Hollywood centers on the NoHo Arts District around Lankershim and Magnolia, with small theaters and the B Line subway terminus, plus a deep bench of Thai, Middle Eastern, Latin and barbecue spots across the wider neighborhood.

gm: Google Maps reviews (local favorites we checked)

places.w: A bright Arts District coffee bar with creative lattes and plenty of dairy-free and sugar-free options.
A bakery cafe with a hidden, plant-filled back patio and generous breakfast plates.
places.o: A pastry and a sandwich out on the patio.

places.w: The Garland hotel's restaurant, with a big courtyard patio and an easy weekend brunch.
places.o: The short rib burger and a martini.

places.w: A small family-run Thai restaurant open since 1984 and one of the most important Thai spots in LA.
places.o: Crispy rice salad and the panang curry.

places.w: Weekend-only Thai street food stalls on the grounds of a Buddhist temple. You trade cash for tokens to pay.
places.o: Arrive before noon, when the popular stalls start to sell out.

places.w: Texas-style barbecue smoked in the alley out back, mostly for takeout.
places.o: Brisket, ribs and burnt ends with the baked beans.

places.w: A busy, multi-room sushi restaurant where the bar is the place to sit.
places.o: Nigiri at the bar, plus the spicy tuna crispy rice.

places.w: A Lebanese restaurant with a garden patio and bread baked fresh in an outdoor oven.
places.o: Kebab platters and the hot mezze.

places.w: One of LA's few Puerto Rican restaurants, with friendly servers who walk first-timers through the menu.
places.o: The appetizer platter, then a carne guisada mofongo.

places.w: A restored 1940s bar in a building shaped like a giant barrel, with a big patio and solid bar food.
places.o: Happy hour out on the patio.

places.w: A restored 1920s theater in the Arts District hosting plays, musicals and concerts.
places.o: Grab a drink at the theater's bar before the show.
